key_insight: Bayesian inference on photoluminescence images and drift-diffusion simulations can localize perovskite solar cell degradation to specific interfaces or the bulk.
engineering_relevance: The method helps engineers identify the dominant failure mode in each device region, guiding targeted stability improvements and passivation strategies.
method: Collect photoluminescence images from fully fabricated perovskite solar cells.
Fit drift-diffusion simulations with Bayesian inference to generate spatial parameter maps.
Track inferred maps over aging under 70 °C full-spectrum sunlight to separate interface vs bulk degradation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports temporally evolving inferred maps with strong spatial heterogeneity and clear degradation at perovskite/transport-layer interfaces, reduced by amino-silane passivation.
watch_item: Inference quality depends on the fidelity of the optical-to-device model; mismatched assumptions could blur the distinction between interface and bulk degradation.
paper_title: Disentangling the origin of degradation in perovskite solar cells via optical imaging and Bayesian inference
